findings.body:
**`test_exact_ack_persists_before_event_...` passes if `event` is never called (apps/crq-python/test_promotion_policy.py:213-228).**

The persistence-before-event check runs only inside the `observed_event` side effect. If `crq.admin` stops emitting `admin_promotion_audit_ack`, the side effect never runs. Every other assertion in the test still holds, so the test passes and the persist-before-emit ordering goes unchecked.

Assert that the event fired exactly once after `self.ack()`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         self.effects["event"].side_effect = observed_event
         self.ack()
+        self.effects["event"].assert_called_once()
         q = self.load()
```
</details>
findings.title: `testexactackpersistsbeforeevent...` passes if `event` is never called (apps/crq-python/testpromotionpolicy.py:213-228).

findings.body:
**Fail the fixture if the `POLICY_FLOOR` pin does not match.**

`test_deploy_controller.py:1282-1284` uses `str.replace` with the literal `POLICY_FLOOR = 'f748fd43...'`. If `prepare-host.py` changes the floor SHA or the quote style, `replace` does nothing and gives no error. The subprocess then runs against the production floor instead of `self.before`. The CLI tests in `test_switch_cli_*` then fail later with a policy-floor refusal that does not point to the cause. A related risk is that the tests could pass without exercising the intended floor. Check that the pin string appears exactly once before you rewrite it.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         original = helper.read_text()
-        helper.write_text(original.replace(
-            "POLICY_FLOOR = 'f748fd43e75505f4e89098a4ffe28fa2a179a50c'",
-            "POLICY_FLOOR = '" + self.before + "'"))
+        pin = "POLICY_FLOOR = 'f748fd43e75505f4e89098a4ffe28fa2a179a50c'"
+        self.assertEqual(original.count(pin), 1,
+                         "prepare-host.py POLICY_FLOOR literal changed; update fixture pin")
+        helper.write_text(original.replace(pin, "POLICY_FLOOR = '" + self.before + "'"))
```
</details>
findings.title: Fail the fixture if the `POLICYFLOOR` pin does not match.

findings.body:
**Add a `timeout=` bound to the `run_cli` subprocess call.**

`run_cli` in `test_deploy_controller.py:1239-1243` calls `subprocess.run` without `timeout`. Health tests run the real `health` command. Its first observation calls `wait_for_first_tick`, which polls until the tick advances or `first_tick_timeout_seconds` expires. A stale heartbeat never advances, so that test waits the full first-tick timeout. The second observation then sleeps `interval_seconds` before it reads. The controller bounds these waits. A CLI that blocks outside them has no bound in the test.

Set the timeout above `first_tick_timeout_seconds` plus `interval_seconds`. A shorter value makes the normal health wait raise `TimeoutExpired`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         return subprocess.run(
             ["python3", "-B", str(OPS / "deploy-controller.py"),
              "--root", str(self.root), "--overlay", str(self.overlay_path),
              "--record-dir", str(self.record_dir), *args],
-            capture_output=True, text=True, env=merged)
+            capture_output=True, text=True, env=merged, timeout=CLI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
```

Define `CLI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` above that value in the test module.
</details>
findings.title: Add a `timeout=` bound to the `runcli` subprocess call.
